To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the mass-radius correlation of neutron stars is sensitive to the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy, and 2) the moment of inertia, the elliptical deformation and the gravitational radiation of rotating neutron stars are sensitive to the density and temperature dependences of the nuclear symmetry free energy.

the density-dependent EOS of nuclear symmetry energy can be constrained by analyzing isospin effects of heavy-ion reactions, which in turn affects neutron stars' properties, such as their mass-radius correlation, moment of in- ertia, elliptical deformation, and gravitational radiation.

the density dependence of the symmetry energy at subsaturation densities is constrained by recent isospin effects observed in heavy-ion reactions and that this constraint is consistent with the EOS of symmetric nuclear matter at sub-sat- uration densities constrained by the elliptic flow of nucleons in relativistic heavy- ion collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the nuclear symmetry energy at low density, which is a fundamental ingredient in the nuclear EOS and has a profound impact on the properties of neutron-rich matter in astrophysical objects such as neutron stars.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EOS of neutron rich matter at densities above saturation density is not well constrained by the present experimental information, and thus the EOS of neutron star crusts, as well as the properties of neutron stars, is still very much model dependent.
the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy is constrained to be rather stiff at sub-sat- uration densities, but it is not yet known how stiff it is at suprasaturation densities.

the density dependence of the symmetry energy at sub- saturation densities has been partially constrained by recent experimental data, and that the EOS of neutron- rich matter is thus partially con- strained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partially constrained EOS is able to reproduce most properties of neutron stars, except for the maximum mass of neutron stars.
the EOS of neutron- rich nuclear matter is constrained by heavy-ion reactions and the EOS of neutron stars can be partially constrained by heavy-ion collisions.

the partially constrained EOS has little effect on the mass-radius relation and elliptical deformation of non-rotating neutron stars, but it does affect the moment of inertia of rotating neutron stars, especially those rotating rapidly, and it also has significant effects on the gravitational radiation of rapidly rotating neutron stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the EOS of symmetric nuclear matter has a large impact on the moment of inertia, the EOS of asymmetric nuclear matter has a larger impact on the mass-radius correlation.
the EOS of neutron- rich nuclear matter at sub-sat- uration densities can be partially constrained by heavy-ion reactions and the constraint is important for the understanding of neutron stars.

the EOS of neutron rich matter at sub-satuation densities has a profound impact on neutron star properties, and thus the density dependence of the symmetry energy at sub- saturation densities can be probed with neutron star observables.
